newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine wheat trade nervous about frost.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat trade nervous about frost.

text.p: Argentine wheat traders said Monday that weekend frosts which hit the southern wheat belt may have caused significant damage to some crops in the area.
But traders and analysts preached caution in assessing any damage and some said the cold snap might have hit too early in the crop's cycle to do much harm.
But one trader said he thought the damage might turn out to be important: "I think there were losses of between 200,000 and 400,000 tonnes."
But he said, "Any damage won't be seen for seven days, if the crop goes white. It looks like the wheat maturing but it's frost damage."
The frosts were most severe in southern Buenos Aires proivince where wheat plants have not yet reached flowering and are less vulnerable.
The trader said he was still assuming a crop of at least 14 million tonnes and pointed out that weather up until now had been very good in the bulk of the wheat belt.

"Everyone in the market has been working with 14 million tonnes to 14.5 million tonnes, but that may turn out to have been conservative," he said, "what with the rise in fertilizer use and the generally good weather."
He added copious rain in the north had led some farmers to take precautions against possible outbreaks of fungus.

Armando Casalins, an analyst of the Grain Elevators Association, said that he thought the frost damage was small: "There was a frost, but I don't think there was any real damage. If the frost had hit further north where the crop is more advanced it would have caused damage."
Most analysts recently have said they expect wheat output to soar this season from last year's drought-blighted total of a bit over nine million tonnes.
The first harvesting in northern areas is due to start in the next few weeks, but the bulk of the crop is brought in in December and January.
